prize_parts.citation: For a visionary body of prose and poetry in Romanian in which memory, the body and metaphysical speculation are built into an expansive, densely patterned imaginative architecture.

statement.case_for: My laureate is unchanged: Cărtărescu (B016). The case rests on the common criteria. The voice is distinctive; on public knowledge the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid join memory, the body, dream and cosmological speculation in long, recursive, patterned prose. The formal ambition has been sustained over decades and at large scale, and the lyric origins in the poetry give the prose its rhythmic and imagistic character. On the chair's scope question, I would anchor the citation in the major prose, with the poetry named as its lyric foundation, so that it does not claim more than the translated corpus lets the committee assess. It would still be a whole-oeuvre citation naming one writer and one language. The six first-place openings are not evidence, and I give them no weight. What persuades me is that the reservations my colleagues and I raised (translation, repetition, uneven coverage of poetry and early work) are the same ones I would raise against any large-scale prose project. None of them has produced a rival whose literary case is clearly stronger on voice, form, depth and sustained achievement. My knowledge comes from public reputation and translation, not from verified reading of the Romanian originals.
statement.case_against: As chair I should state the strongest case against my own preferred candidate, since the chair summary asked who would do so. First, the claim to a distinctive voice rests largely on Romanian syntax, wordplay and rhythm, and a committee reading in translation may be judging an approximation. A recognisable architecture of imagery and structure is not the same thing as a recognisable language, and the criteria concern language. Second, recurrence of motifs across very long books may be a closed circuit, and we have not tested it against specific volumes. Third, the poetry and early work are thinly available, so a whole-oeuvre claim is weaker than a claim for the major novels. Fourth, unanimity in the openings means the committee has not yet been put to a test it could fail. If the committee cannot obtain an assessment from a Romanian-language reader, which the regional-expert practice is meant to provide, the claim stays provisional. A prize resting on a style we cannot read directly would then be less secure than our shared confidence suggests.

responses.point: Carlberg ranked Zurita eighth. She says poetry in translation is the least secure basis for judgment, and that landscape-scale interventions and the political and historical context make it hard to isolate the language itself.
responses.response: That is a fair criticism of my opening ranking, and it changes part of my configuration. I ranked Zurita second because the poetic project in Purgatory and Anteparadise seemed to me among the most ambitious on the list. But my own caution applies to him as much as to anyone, and I have not shown which poems carry the case on the page. Poetry that depends on its relation to a collective historical catastrophe is hard to separate from that context when read in translation. I therefore withdraw Zurita from my alternatives. I do not think the work is lesser. I cannot currently state a citation that rests on the printed poems alone, and an alternative I cannot defend in that way should not be offered. I accept Carlberg's point on weight, though I still think the poetry deserves a closer reading than the openings gave it.

responses.point: Palm argues that Cărtărescu's effect depends more on large-scale architecture and imagery, which survive translation better, than Michon's depends on syntax and cadence.
responses.response: I accept this as a difference of degree and I used a similar argument in round 1. I now want to test it. Architecture and imagery may survive translation, but the claim in our citation is to voice and linguistic achievement, and those are carried by sentence-level texture as well as structure. So the argument protects Cărtărescu from a comparison with Michon without establishing that the language itself is rendered well. I would not use it to close the translation question. It is a reason to expect the translations to carry more of the achievement than they would for Michon, and the Romanian-language assessment is still needed to confirm it. I agree with Palm that the case has a clear attributable scope, one writer in one language, and that helps the citation.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg reads the major books as reorganising the same materials at different scales and in different forms, which he calls development, not repetition. He grounds the case in the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid.
responses.response: This is the most useful answer to the chair's question about which books to test against. It suggests comparing the Blinding trilogy with Solenoid. If the later book rebuilds the same materials of memory, the body and dream under a different structure and narrative stance, that supports development. If it reuses the trilogy's procedures at larger scale, Palm's and Carlberg's worry about a closed circuit gains force. I cannot settle this from public knowledge. My provisional view is that the reorganisation does look like widening, but that is a reading from reputation. I would ask any member who has read both to say specifically what changes between them, and I would not move on this point from assertion alone.

responses.point: Mattson says a citation for Michon must be precise about what is honoured, the invention of a form of fictional lives, and keeps him as her first alternative. She also asks which poems carry the Zurita case on the page.
responses.response: I take the second question as answered by my previous reply: I cannot yet name the poems and have withdrawn Zurita as an alternative. On Michon I agree with her wording. The case is a form, fictional lives built from compressed, rhythmically exact prose, and that is a clear citation scope. My difficulty is the one we both name. A compact corpus gives less evidence of sustained quality and development, and the loss in translation is greatest where the achievement is cadence. I still do not think that excludes him, and I would not regard a Michon recommendation as an error, but I judge the scale evidence for Cărtărescu stronger. I list Michon as a second alternative because his case is the clearest to state.

uncertainties: Whether the available translations carry the patterning, wordplay and rhythm of Cărtărescu's Romanian well enough to support a judgment of language, and whether a Romanian-language expert assessment would confirm it. I have not obtained or verified such an assessment.
Whether the later large novels widen the project or reuse its procedures at larger scale; the comparison between the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid has not been tested by anyone in the record.
How much of the poetry and early work is translated, and so whether the citation can responsibly name poetry beyond calling it a lyric foundation.

If translation obscures too much, I have made Carson my first fallback because the committee can read her English directly. Whether a citation can define her contribution without depending on book design, scholarship or translation remains unresolved.
Michon's compact corpus and the uncertain translation of his syntax limit what can be said about range and development; my knowledge of both is from public reputation, not direct reading.
I cannot state which of Zurita's poems carry a case on the page, so I have withdrawn him as an alternative; this reflects the limits of my evidence, not a settled view on the work.
My knowledge rests on public reputation and the colleagues' stated assessments, not on independent verification of any text.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My scholarly work on modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature and Celan is context only; the profile records no tie to any shortlisted writer, and my own practice is not evidence of preference. As chair I wrote the round-1 summary and posed its questions. That role carries a duty to keep scrutiny of the shared reservations from being shortened, but it gives me no additional weight on the merits. Carlberg's voting status as a co-opted member is undocumented and her simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
